sections.html:
Marion County's seat is also Oregon's capital, in the north-central Willamette Valley. The Willamette flows north through the middle of town and doubles as the Marion-Polk line, which puts West Salem in Polk County and nearly everything else in Marion.

For a seller, that line is practical. A house in West Salem and one east of the river can both carry a Salem address yet use different county offices, tax collectors and recording steps. Confirm your side of the river first, then call the matching office.

The 2020 count was 175,535 residents, second only to Portland among Oregon cities. The city covers about 49.6 square miles and has 17 recognized neighborhood associations. Elevation runs from roughly 120 to 800 feet, so some lots are flat valley floor and others sit on slopes.

Winters here are wet and summers dry, and precipitation totals 40.08 inches a year, mostly October through April. For a sale, flooding counts for more than heat.

  • 1861: the largest Willamette flood on record.
  • 1964: the Christmas flood crested nearly ten feet above flood stage, caused $157 million in damage and killed 20 Oregonians.
  • February 1996: flood levels near the 100-year mark.
  • January 2012: more than nine inches of rain in five days in south Salem flooded the Battle Creek, Mill Creek, Pringle Creek and Croisan Creek basins, with about 300 evacuated and 64 streets closed.

City staff can say if a parcel is inside the FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area or the floodway, and the city maintains both a flood insurance rate map and an interactive floodplain map. Call Development Services at 503-584-4646. Near a creek? Get that answer before you pick a closing date. The city's flood history page has more.

On a Salem house, the questions to answer most carefully are floodplain status, creek drainage and past water damage. Collect repair invoices, photos and insurance paperwork. Inspectors will poke around the basement, crawlspace and lowest floor, and tidy records cut that conversation short.

The Marion County bill for a Salem house splits into three installments: November 15, February 15 and May 15. If one of those dates lands on a weekend or holiday, payment is due the next business day. West Salem pays through the Polk County tax office.

Payment optionDue dateDiscount
Pay in fullNovember 153%
Pay two-thirdsNovember 152% on the amount paid
Pay one-thirdNovember 15None

Anything postmarked late forfeits the discount and picks up interest.

• By mail: Marion County Tax Collection, PO Box 3416, Portland, OR 97208-3416.
  • Online or by phone: Paystation, as listed on the county's payment page.
  • In person: Courthouse Square, 555 Court Street NE, with after-hours drop boxes.
  • Questions: 503-588-5215.

Under Measure 50, assessed value generally cannot grow more than about 3 percent a year, so a house owned since the 1990s often has an assessed value far below market. The county payment page has the details.

sections.h2: What a Salem seller must disclose
sections.html:
Sellers hand a property disclosure statement to every buyer who writes an offer, and that buyer may revoke within five days of delivery. Topics include title, water, sewage, structure, systems, seismic issues and general conditions.

ORS 105.470 lets a court-appointed personal representative, trustee, conservator or guardian, or a financial institution selling after foreclosure, complete only the short Section 1.

sections.h2: Getting around, and why buyers care
sections.html: Interstate 5 runs through Salem, along with Oregon Routes 99E, 22, 221, 51 and 213. Route 22 crosses the river into West Salem on the Marion Street and Center Street bridges. Cherriots runs the local buses, and Amtrak stops at the Salem station. Mention commute options in the listing, since many buyers work for the state or at the hospital.

sections.h2: Selling a Salem house for cash
sections.html:
Cash means no lender, which removes the appraisal and underwriting stages.

  1. Give the address, the state of the house and when you hope to close.
  2. Read the offer in writing, including closing costs and who handles repairs.
  3. A title company opens escrow and screens for liens and back taxes.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and proceeds are paid out.

Floodplain status and water history are checked during escrow, so it helps to answer those questions at the start.

Anything overdue is deducted from your proceeds when you close, interest included. Request a payoff number from the title company, or phone 503-588-5215 to see what Marion County has on record. In West Salem, ask the Polk County tax office instead.

• Photo ID matching the deed.
  • The latest tax statement.
  • Lender and loan number if there is a mortgage.
  • Records of any water damage repair.
  • Lease papers if a tenant lives there.

sections.h2: Preparing a house near a creek
sections.html: Does your lot border one of Salem's creek basins? Start with the work buyers can see. Clear storm drains and gutters, make sure downspouts carry water away from the foundation, and check the crawlspace or basement for damp spots and old stains. Fix what is cheap to fix. For anything larger, get a written estimate, because a buyer who sees a number is calmer than one who only sees a stain.

When a court-appointed personal representative or trustee is the seller, the shortened disclosure form may apply. Even so, collect the court papers that prove authority to sign, an up-to-date tax statement and any notes on the house's condition. The title company will ask for them, and having them early prevents a stall at escrow. If the house sits on the Polk County side, confirm which recording office handles the deed.

A title or escrow company handles the signing. Both sides sign, the deed is recorded, and your mortgage payoff, any unpaid taxes and the split of the current tax year come out of the price. The remainder is yours. With no lender on the buyer's side, the closing date can follow your moving plans instead of a bank's schedule.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the rainy season
sections.html: Because most of the year's precipitation arrives between October and April, a house listed in winter shows its drainage honestly, and buyers see how it handles a storm. If that is your timing, make sure gutters are clear and any sump or drain works. If you can wait until the dry months, a lot that tends to hold water looks better, though the disclosure form still asks about past problems either way.

faqs.a: No. Salem is the seat of Marion County, and the river is the line with Polk County. West Salem lies in Polk County, so tax and recording offices can differ across the river.

faqs.q: When are Marion County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15, February 15 and May 15. A full payment by November 15 earns a 3 percent discount, and two-thirds earns 2 percent. If the date lands on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.
Yes. The Willamette flooded in 1861, the Christmas flood of 1964 crested nearly ten feet above flood stage, and January 2012 rains flooded several south Salem creek basins and closed 64 streets.

faqs.q: How do I find out if my Salem house is in a floodplain?
faqs.a: Ask the city. Development Services at 503-584-4646 can tell you whether a parcel is in the FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area or the floodway.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Salem house with water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. You disclose what you know on the Oregon seller's form, and a cash buyer prices the house as it stands. Floodplain status can be checked with the city's Development Services office.
